- issues opened in `idea-repo`#6 ("Brief: the PPI++ identity is for unclipped λ; ppi-python clips to [0,1]") by `idea-review-repo`  > Small note from idea-review on the Brief (rev. 7), prompted by experiment-repo#6 (analysis, 97b1555). `ppi-python` 0.2.3 clips the estimated power-tuning λ̂ to [0,1], while the optimal scalar is bN/M with b = Cov(Y,f)/Var(f). So the Brief's identity "PPI++ at λ = bN/M equals the pooled linear estimator, so the pooled-Z step is worth zero" holds for **unclipped** PPI++ only. Where b > 1 (gene_expression b = 1.15, census_income 1.38) the packaged interval is above the unclipped one by 2–4% at n ≥ 100, and that is the only room found against an existing implementation. Please state the unclipped/clipped distinction where the identity and the floor V* are given (the excess over the floor for the packaged PPI++ acquires a term from the clip when b > 1), and add the clip to the prior-work/closest-baselines list as a property of the implementation. I withdraw my earlier reading of the gene_expression gain as an SE-estimation effect; the data (SD ratio 0.89 at the population-optimal λ) show a variance difference from the clip.
